title.narrative: PMNCH - Safeguarding gains and accelerating progress on SRHR

description.narrative:
The Partnership for Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (PMNCH) is advancing efforts to safeguard and accelerate progress on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) through an integrated advocacy approach. With a focus on women, children, and adolescents, the project aims to address challenges posed by anti-rights movements, insufficient funding, and policy gaps that threaten years of progress. PMNCH’s work aligns with the SDGs and leverages its extensive network of global, regional, and national partners.
Main Objectives The project’s overarching impact includes improving SRHR outcomes, reducing maternal and child morbidity and mortality, and enhancing adolescent well-being. To achieve this, the project focuses on three key advocacy outcomes: 1. Containing opposition to SRHR, supporting progressive policies, and countering misinformation. 2. Increasing domestic and donor financing for SRHR interventions and commodities. 3. Mainstreaming SRHR within national, regional, and global health systems, including Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and Primary Health Care (PHC).
Main Activities and Workstreams PMNCH’s work is organized into four interconnected workstreams, each tailored to achieve the desired advocacy outcomes. 1. Implementing Advocacy for Accountability (CAAPs) 2. Global-South Led Global Leaders Network (GLN) 3. Creating and Empowering a Coalition of SRHR Advocates 4. Working with the African Union (AU)
The project primarily targets women, children, and adolescents, especially in low- and middle-income countries. It also engages local and national governments, youth-led organizations, and civil society actors, as well as global and regional political leaders, particularly from the Global South.
